mx.intro_one: Before you can receive emails for your custom domain addresses at Kutup Mail, you need to add the following MX record in your DNS console (located on the platform where you purchased the custom domain).
mx.intro_other: Before you can receive emails for your custom domain addresses at Kutup Mail, you need to add the following {{count}} MX records in your DNS console (located on the platform where you purchased the custom domain).

spf.intro: SPF clarifies who is allowed to send email for your domain. Make sure you add the following TXT record in your DNS console (located on the platform where you purchased the custom domain).
spf.merge: Each domain can only have one SPF (TXT) record. If you want to keep the existing SPF (TXT) record, you can add {{include}} to your current record (put it after {{start}}).

dkim.intro_one: DKIM allows Kutup to cryptographically sign your emails and prevent attackers from tampering your email. Make sure you add the following CNAME record in your DNS console (located on the platform where you purchased the custom domain).
dkim.intro_other: DKIM allows Kutup to cryptographically sign your emails and prevent attackers from tampering your email. Make sure you add the following {{count}} CNAME records in your DNS console (located on the platform where you purchased the custom domain).
dkim.ask_one: Please add the following CNAME record. Note: DNS records can take several hours to update.
dkim.ask_other: Please add all {{count}} of the following CNAME records. Note: DNS records can take several hours to update.
dkim.error: We stopped DKIM signing due to problems with your DNS configuration. Please follow the instructions below to resume signing.
dkim.warning: We detected a problem with your DNS configuration. Please make sure your records match the instructions below. If the problem persists, we will have to switch DKIM signing off.
dkim.dot: IMPORTANT: If your DNS console does not allow CNAME values to end with a dot, you can remove the last dot in the CNAME values.

dmarc.intro: DMARC checks if the sender's SPF and DKIM records originate from your domain. This can prevent attackers from using another domain's SPF and DKIM to impersonate your domain. The "p=" (policy) in this record indicates how you want the recipient platforms to handle unauthorized emails. We recommend using the "p=quarantine" policy for most domains. Make sure you add the following TXT record in your DNS console (located on the platform where you purchased the custom domain).
dmarc.quarantine: {{policy}}: asking the recipient platforms to mark the unauthorized emails as spam or quarantine them.
dmarc.reject: {{policy}}: asking the recipient platforms to reject the unauthorized emails.
dmarc.none: {{policy}}: do not quarantine or reject unauthorized emails. Usually, people only use this policy to troubleshoot or test.

catchAll.title: Catch-all address
catchAll.description: Mail sent to an address on this domain that doesn't exist (e.g., because of typos) goes to the catch-all address.
